```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)
```

#loading libraries needed for pipeline
```{r}
library(phyloseq)
library(Biostrings)
require(tidyverse)
require(compositions)
require(ALDEx2)
require(FactoMineR)
require(factoextra)
library(reshape2)
conflicted::conflict_prefer("select", "dplyr")
conflicted::conflict_prefer("filter", "dplyr")
```

#------Pre-processing-----
#prepare phyloseq object 
```{r}
#for this step look at DADA2 pipeline; refered to as physeq_merge
#remove PEG and Redo data
new_phyloseq <- subset_samples(physeq_merge, !(Location %in% c("PEG", "Redo")))
```

#tax glom genus data
```{r}
ps_genus_2 <- tax_glom(new_phyloseq, "Genus")
```

#convert phyloseq object to matrix
```{r}
ps_genus_2_mat <- as(otu_table(ps_genus_2), "matrix")
```

#check column and row names of matrix
```{r}
#column names should be samples, row names should be ASVs
colnames(ps_genus_2_mat)
rownames(ps_genus_2_mat)
```

#------CODA-----
#transpose abundance data for CoDA
```{r}
#Before: rows = families, columns = samples
#After:  rows = samples, columns = families
Orddf4aldex <- t(ps_genus_2_mat)

#Check to see if the transposing worked 
colnames(Orddf4aldex)
rownames(Orddf4aldex)

#Check for values between 0 and 1
sum(Orddf4aldex > 0 & Orddf4aldex < 1)
#Check whether all values are whole numbers
all(Orddf4aldex %% 1 == 0)
```

#Creating a new object for downstream analysis
```{r}
subset_aldex <- Orddf4aldex
```

#Checks whether any values are between 0 and 1, if so multiplies them by 10,000 to ensure they are pseudo whole number for downstream analysis aka CZM
```{r}
if (sum(Orddf4aldex > 0 & Orddf4aldex < 1) > 0) {
  subset_aldex <- round(Orddf4aldex * 10000, 0)
} else {
  subset_aldex <- Orddf4aldex
}
```

#Replace zeros using Count Zero Multiplicative replacement (no. adjusted imputations = 105)
```{r}
Ord_clr <- cmultRepl(
  subset_aldex,
  method = "CZM",
  output = "p-counts"
)
```

#----Quick Check
```{r}
# Number of zeros before
sum(subset_aldex == 0)

# Number of zeros after
sum(Ord_clr == 0)

# Check for any negative values
sum(Ord_clr < 0)

# View the result
View(Ord_clr)
```

#Conversion of samples to proportions. (For Sequencing Depth)
```{r}
#This step converts the raw counts or pseudo counts into proportions by dividing each taxon's abundance by the total number of reads in that sample.
Ord_clr <- apply(
  Ord_clr,
  1,
  function(x) x / sum(x)
)
```

#CLR Transformation
#What the code does is for each sample it takes the natural log of each taxon's proportion
#and subtract the average log abundance (the log of the geometric mean).
#This expresses each taxon's abundance relative to the average taxon. This does it on a column basis as seen by 2 in the apply function,within the sample
```{r}
Ord_clr <- apply(
  Ord_clr,
  2,
  function(x) log(x) - mean(log(x))
)
```

#Checking if it worked(s) and no valid finite numbers
```{r}
colSums(Ord_clr)
sum(!is.finite(Ord_clr))
```

#------Plotting PCA (using factoextra package)-----
#transpose clr object from CODA
```{r}
Ord_clr_t <- t(Ord_clr)
```

#run PCA on transposed object
```{r}
res_pca <- PCA(Ord_clr_t, scale.unit = FALSE, graph = FALSE)
```

#add taxa back to ASVs
```{r}
#pull taxa from tax_glom genus phylseq object
tax_pca <- as.data.frame(phyloseq::tax_table(ps_genus_2))

#pull ASV names in PCA
asv_pca <- rownames(res_pca$var$coord)

#match pulled genus taxa to ASVs
asv_identify <- tax_pca[asv_pca, "Genus"]

#assign taxa to various PCA results
rownames(res_pca$var$coord)  <- asv_identify
rownames(res_pca$var$contrib) <- asv_identify
rownames(res_pca$var$cos2)    <- asv_identify
```

#add metadata for graphing
```{r}
metadata <- read.csv (file = "C:/Users/cjm30/Bioinformatics/V4V5_metagenomics/McKellarV4V5/metadata.csv")#change file path for personal computer

meta_2 <- metadata %>% filter(!Location %in% c("Redo", "PEG"))
```

#manually calculate variance in PCA (allows you to alter axis labels in PCA plots)
```{r}
#Create PCA input table
PCA_input <- as.data.frame(t(Ord_clr)) %>%
  rownames_to_column ("ID") %>%
  left_join(
  meta_2 %>%
  select(ID, Date, Location_2, Type),
  by = "ID"
  )

#Separate CLR-transformed family data from metadata
PCA_input <- PCA_input %>%
  select(-ID, -Date, -Location_2, -Type)

#do PCA 
PCA_output <- prcomp(
  PCA_input,
  center = TRUE,
  scale. = FALSE
)

#calculate variance
variance_explained <- (PCA_output$sdev^2 / sum(PCA_output$sdev^2)) * 100
```

#graph biplot of individuals and variables (PC1 and PC2) (for all samples, as example)
#looked at 20 contrib for variables
#ellipse has an 80% CI
```{r}
fviz_pca_biplot(res_pca, 
      geom.ind = "point",
      axes = c(1, 2),
      fill.ind = meta_2$Location_2, col.ind = "white",
      repel = TRUE,
      pointshape = 21, pointsize = 3,arrowsize = 1,labelsize = 3.5,
      palette = "jco",
      addEllipses = TRUE,ellipse.level=0.80,
      select.var = list(contrib = 20),
      col.var = "contrib",
      gradient.cols = "Dark2",
)+
  labs(fill = "Location", color = "Contrib",
       x = paste0("PC1 (", round(variance_explained[1], 1), "%)"),
       y = paste0("PC2 (", round(variance_explained[2], 1), "%)"),
       title = NULL)

#to save graph
ggsave("PCA_results_location_threetypes.png", plot = last_plot(), width = 9, height = 8, dpi = 300)
```

#graph individuals (PC1 and PC2) (for all samples based on location, as example)
```{r}
fviz_pca_ind(res_pca,
            geom.ind = c("point","text"),
            repel = TRUE, 
            col.ind = meta_2$Location_2,
            pointsize = 3,labelsize = 5,
            addEllipses=TRUE, ellipse.level=0.95, 
            palette = "jco", 
            legend.title = "Location")+
  labs(colour = "Location",
       x = paste0("PC1 (", round(variance_explained[1], 1), "%)"),
       y = paste0("PC2 (", round(variance_explained[2], 1), "%)"))+
  theme(
    axis.title = element_text(size = 16),
    axis.text  = element_text(size = 14),
    legend.text = element_text(size = 12),
    legend.title = element_text(size = 14)
  )
```
